newsitem.title: USA: Seagate sees no slowing in business market.
newsitem.headline: Seagate sees no slowing in business market.

text.p: SAN FRANCISCO, Calif., Feb 27 - Seagate Technology Inc Chairman and CEO Alan Shugart said the company expects to recoup market share it lost in the December quarter in desktop systems and sees no slowdown in high-end servers.
The Scotts Valley-based maker of disk drive and data storage products is also likely to make more software acquisitions, he said, but he declined to elaborate.
Shugart, who made the comments in a presentation at the Robertson Stephens technology conference, later told reporters not to expect such acquisitions this quarter.
Shugart said business in the high-performance server market where Seagate is a dominant supplier "hasn't slowed down at all. I don't see any slowdown in the foreseeable future."

Shugart said the company had lost some market share in its desktop storage systems area in its second fiscal quarter to the end of December, largely due to a shortage of components as the industry was facing a shortage of magnetic recording heads.
But he expressed confidence that Seagate could regain that lost share.
"The demand is so big," he said. "We lost between three and four percent of market share in the desktop market, which we're looking to gain back."
He said the demand for magnetic recording devices continues to rise, but he felt capacity was being built up sufficiently to meet demand by the end of Seagate's fiscal year on June 30.
"I think that will all be solved before June -- sometime between March and June," he said.

The silver lining in the desktop systems business was that, with benefits in absorption of Seagate's acquisition of Conner Peripherals, the company was able to improve margins in its desktop business.

Shugart said the good news in the business area is that "gross margins went up dramatically" and he told reporters after the presentation he expects gross margins in the business could be improved by up to six percentage points over the next two quarters.
He declined to say what the gross margin levels are for the business, however.

"There will be some more acquisitions in the software area," said Shugart, noting the company's software revenues rose to $55 million in its second fiscal quarter. "I can't tell you now who, when, what or where but there will be more."
He said the desktop computer market growth is being driven by adaption of Microsoft Corp's Windows NT product.

"What's really driving the desktop computer market I believe is Windows NT at the corporate client level," he said. "In my discussions with other companies around the world, that is the big driving force behind the sales of desktop PCs.
"I don't think the home market is growing like the corporate market is growing," he added.
Shugart said the company will also concentrate on raising its share of the mobile computing storage marketplace.

"We've done poorly with mobile. We expect to do better. We've reorganized the operation. We will hopefully take that four to six percent (market share) up to the 15 percent range in the next two quarters," he said.
"The mobile market should be an area where we make some money," he said.
((sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400))
